name: Black Nosed Dace
imitates: A slim bucktail minnow imitation, classic in the East and a good small trailer fly behind a heavier pattern.
recipe: White, black and brown bucktail, layered

steps.text: Wrap a thread base behind the return wire, tie in a strand of red Darlon on top of the shank and wrap back over it to the bend. Trim the tail to about one gap width later.
Tie in flat mylar tinsel gold side up, wrap back to the tail, then fold it and wrap forward silver side up in tight, slightly overlapping turns. Tie off.
Trim the tinsel stub and build a smooth thread base from the body to the eye, leaving a small gap behind the eye for a clean head later.
Tie in a sparse, unstacked clump of white bucktail with a narrow band at the front of the body, tips just past the tail.
Trim the butts at an angle so they form a ramp, then smooth a thread base over them.
Tie in an equally sparse clump of black bucktail on top of the white, the same length, and trim the butts at an angle.
Tie in a like-sized clump of brown bucktail on top, keeping the thread wraps toward the rear, and cut the butts at a slightly steeper angle.
Build a smooth, slightly tapered thread head over the butts, whip finish and coat the head with two layers of lacquer.
Finished Black Nosed Dace: slim silver body, red tail, white belly, black lateral line and brown back.
